title: TO MY VELUTHA
author: Heba Fatima
text:
There is a sorrow in me that grows,
swells like the belly of a pregnant woman.
tomorrow.
the fungi-infested bark, with blossoms of white gossamer
here and there
like our memories,
waits patiently,
unlike me.
`tomorrow`
it whispers into the ears of ladybugs,
sleepy ladybugs filling with hope
moment by moment,
like me.

the moon that waxes at your sight,
waning with your retracting footsteps
when you turn and carve your lips into a word
and i, blurry-eyed,
always know.
"tomorrow"
the moon, its
craters full of sorrow, expanding.
Ripples in the water,
ripples in my heart.
The waters rising,
like a woman to avenge her disgrace
at the hands of hundred men,
or a hundred and five.
its ravenous claws clutching
at the shore,
carrying it home,
like children stuffing sand in their pockets.
this shore
our home of memories.

the belly grows,
never bursting.
always accumulating.
what if tomorrow
there is no shore?
what if tomorrow
there is no tomorrow?
stanzas: There is a sorrow in me that grows,
swells like the belly of a pregnant woman.
the fungi-infested bark, with blossoms of white gossamer
it whispers into the ears of ladybugs,
the moon that waxes at your sight,
when you turn and carve your lips into a word
like a woman to avenge her disgrace
at the hands of hundred men,
like children stuffing sand in their pockets.
